_comment: The design families, and the ONLY place their flags are written down.
build.ps1 builds from this file and check_design_sets.py verifies the
built sets against it, so there is no second copy to drift. It used to be
five pasteable commands in README.md, which cost three separate people a
session: a <dst> placeholder PowerShell rejects as a reserved operator, a
$dst variable it silently expands to nothing (building to the DRIVE ROOT),
and two pasted in parallel, which corrupt each other's cache entries.
EVERY FLAG IS LOAD-BEARING. A set is selected at load time by hidden,
intermediate, gated_ffn AND the datapath, so a set built with the wrong
flags is not a slower design -- it is one the wrong model loads, or none.
Both directions of that have already shipped wrong once.
_common_note: --tg-depth 2 software-pipelines the runtime sequence's task groups: worth
1.034-1.141x of array time, bit-identical. --tg-depth 3 compiles clean and
then TIMES OUT on hardware, reproducibly. 2 is the maximum that runs.
Four batch tiers, because use_tier() picks the smallest that fits and
falls back to the largest. A single tier pads every request to batch 128:
measured at 18.3x on a single text, with the four-tier design
bit-identical. Upstream's bge-large still ships one tier -- see T66.

families.name: BERT-h384-bf16
families.note: THE ONE FAMILY WITH NEITHER --emulate-bfp16 NOR --c-bf16. bge-small failed the bfp16 MTEB gate at -0.5010 bit-reproducibly, so it stays on the plain datapath, and its C stays fp32. Adding --c-bf16 here builds a design that loads and is not the one that passed the gates -- which shipped once.

families.name: BERT-h768-gated-bfp16
families.note: One set for two models: their GEMM geometry matches bit for bit. Note also that qkv and attn_out here are IDENTICAL to BERT-h768-bfp16's -- neither depends on --gated-ffn or --intermediate -- so these two families share 8 of their 16 cache markers and must never be built concurrently.

families.name: BERT-h1024-bfp16
families.note: -n 32, not 48: the design asserts N % (tile_n * n_cols) == 0 and bge-large's N is in {1024, 3072, 4096}. 64 divides them but needs 65,536 B of a 63 KB L1 budget.
